pairs.subject: copy-quality-gates
pairs.evidence: scripts/data-analysis/kg-forensics.ts:122 The forensic writer calls validateLawVerdict without requireCzech, so the default (law-verdict.ts:298 `opts.requireCzech !== false`) applies: the stopword-rate language classifier in lib/analysis/language-gate.ts (EN_RATE_THRESHOLD = 0.05) can hard-reject a whole verdict. That is a threshold on a score holding the error tier, which the standard says must only warn.

techniques.evidence: scripts/data-analysis/kg-forensics.ts:122 The default requireCzech runs a score-threshold language classifier as a blocking check. The standard says a statistical verdict warns and never blocks.

scripts/data-analysis/kg-forensics.ts:124 Every validator error rejects the verdict alike, and the next line prints only the first four. No rule has a declared disposition, and the error strings carry no rule identifier.

pairs.registryProposal: language-gate.ts is a deterministic stopword-list classifier with a rate threshold. Its false positives do have addresses: a word removed from a list (`evidence` was taken out of the English list on 2026-08-12 after 14 of 211 Czech notes were wrongly withheld). The standard groups 'a threshold on a score' with model verdicts, but its own reason (no address a guard can fix) does not hold for closed-list classifiers. The standard should say which side such a classifier falls on.
